item.title: Wayne Gretzky sees no comparison between Connor McDavid & other NHL stars
item.description: Wayne Gretzky has said that Connor McDavid remains in a class of his own, with the Edmonton Oilers captain producing another remarkable season. After leading the league with 138 points last season, the Oilers captain has registered 55 points so far, including 13 goals and 42 assists with a plus-minus rating of 29. Speaking on NHL on TNT, Gretzky praised McDavid’s scoring pace, leadership, and determination to win the Stanley Cup. He also highlighted Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard as important parts of Edmonton’s success. When Liam McHugh asked whether McDavid looked different this season, Gretzky offered a clear assessment. “Well, I think it’s a combination of things. First, he’s the best player in the game today, right? There’s no comparison,” Gretzky said. Gretzky owns the record with 51 games in 1983-84, while his 30-game streak from 1982-83 shares second place with Mats Sundin. Mario Lemieux also recorded a 46-game point streak during the 1989-90 season, although it did not begin the season. item.title: 'Cummins will struggle to captain Australia': Ian Healy's blunt warning after Bancroft's Sandpapergate revelations
item.description: Former Australia wicketkeeper Ian Healy has warned that Pat Cummins will struggle to lead the Test side unless he directly refutes Cameron Bancroft’s explosive claim that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test. Bancroft, one of the central figures in the Sandpapergate scandal, said on Tuesday that the entire team was aware of the conspiracy but he ended up taking "the bullet" for everyone. His remarks have reignited questions over what happened in South Africa and the credibility of those who maintained they knew nothing about the plot. The latest controversy follows Cummins dismissing former teammate Usman Khawaja's claim in his book that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan as “complete and utter nonsense.” Reacting to Bancroft's fresh allegations, Healy said Cummins needed to address the issue directly if he wanted to retain his authority as captain. "I would feel without refuting Cameron Bancroft's words again, he (Cummins) will struggle to captain the team. “You've had a big part of your credibility taken away with that press conference now that it's been proven to be not as complete as Pat made it out to be,” Healy told SEN. ALSO READ: Cummins under pressure as Bancroft's explosive claims trigger calls for captaincy review Healy says Cummins need not step down Asked whether Cummins should stand down as Australia captain, Healy said he did not believe that was necessary, while questioning the way Cricket Australia had handled the scandal in 2018. "No, he doesn't need to stand down. And I don't want to get into another panic mode of what happened in 2018, it was panic, and they tried to do an investigation in no time, didn't talk to anyone, it was rubbish. It was a lack of quality and rubbish, and rushed, and panicked. "Now, I can't say whether he should stand down now. Will he stand down? That might be a different thing. He might stand down," said the 62-year-old, who played 119 Tests and 168 ODIs between 1988 and 1999. Healy also argued that the latest revelations could damage the personal legacies of Cummins and fellow Australia bowlers Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, who had said they were unaware of the ball-tampering plan. “I would say it taints their personal legacies. I don't think it's going to taint their performance legacies. Personally now, they're not as credible as they once were, unless they change something drastically in the next few days," Healy said. Healy also suggested that the ball-tampering could have been happening for longer than previously believed. “So they probably achieved some success with their skills, with a ball that's doing more than it was going to. item.title: 'Man of integrity' Diallo can restore proper values to FIFA: UEFA vice-president
item.description: French football chief Philippe Diallo (R) can restore values to FIFA that have been lost under the regime of Gianni Infantino (L), said a UEFA vice-president (FRANCK FIFE) French football chief Philippe Diallo's bid to depose Gianni Infantino as FIFA president is less about replacing one man than overhauling how football's governing body has been run under him, a UEFA vice-president told AFP. Laura McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of European football's governing body, said Diallo was a "man of integrity" and his values aligned with UEFA "which it feels are critical to change the governance of FIFA". UEFA have been in the vanguard of opposition to Infantino -- they described his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors as a "shabby, back room, opaque deal". McAllister said although some have dismissed Diallo as a stop-gap candidate, after others such as CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and elder statesman Arsene Wenger opted out, he stood on his "merits". "We knew it would be a tricky process to find an appropriate candidate with regime change and accountability as the programme," she told AFP in a phone interview on Wednesday. "Philippe Diallo can do that adeptly. Were there other candidates mentioned before? Yes there were, but it is now about the timetable of aligning values and articulating them. "It does not matter about who might have been a candidate, this is the here and now and he is a strong and credible values-driven candidate." Diallo and former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima are hoping to dash Infantino's hopes of a fourth and final term in Rabat on March 18 next year. "We respect him a lot, his values align with ours," McAllister said of Tashima. "Let us see how that plays out." McAllister is at pains to insist it is more about changing the system than replacing one person. "It was never about ridding FIFA of one leader, it is about reform of the framework of governance, finance and redistribution system," she said. - 'Patterns of behaviour'- McAllister said Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at an Olympics, should not be seen as solely a European candidate. "He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF (Confederation of African Football) countries," she said. CAF have been among Infantino's most vocal supporters, partly because Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 men's World Cup. The South American governing body CONMEBOL also backs him. More surprising was the Asian Football Confederation's (AFC) volte-face -- having heavily criticised Infantino, they announced last month they supported his re-election. item.title: How a restoration added challenge to Sea Island without changing its soul
item.description: ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. – For years, longtime Sea Island instructor Jack Lumpkin carried around a list of places where he believed the Seaside Course could be lengthened. “Whenever anybody would listen, he'd take us out there and show us, ‘You should back this tee up,’” Davis Love III recalled. Lumpkin passed away several years ago, but his vision has finally become reality. Ahead of this week's RSM Classic, Sea Island unveiled a multi-million-dollar restoration of its famed Seaside Course led by Love Golf Design, headed by Love, his brother, Mark, and lead architect Scott Sherman, in collaboration with MacCurrach Golf Construction. The project was designed to honor the course's architectural heritage while enhancing playability for resort guests and adding subtle challenge for tournament competitors. Originally designed by Harry Colt and Charles Alison in 1929, the Seaside Course underwent a major renovation in 1999 when Tom Fazio combined nine holes from the original Alison layout and nine from a Joe Lee-designed course to create an entirely new 18-hole design. The latest restoration included a complete turf replacement, infrastructure upgrades, dune restoration and a series of strategic refinements throughout the property. “We used historic pictures and Google Earth as a guide to restore Tom Fazio's original vision,” Love said. Among the changes are new back tees on Nos. 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 and 16, adding roughly 150 yards to the par-70 layout, which now stretches to 7,157 yards. Many of those additions trace directly to suggestions Lumpkin championed for years. The project also included installation of a new irrigation system. The greens remain TifEagle Bermudagrass, while the collars, approaches, tees, fairways and rough were converted to Platinum Paspalum, a grass variety prized for its salt tolerance in coastal environments. Some of the most significant architectural changes came on the back nine. At the par-4 10th hole, the green was moved approximately 20 yards farther from the tee and lowered about two feet, with its original contours preserved through digital scanning technology. The par-4 15th also received a substantial makeover. A new back tee lengthened the hole, while the green was shifted closer to the water and lowered slightly. The left greenside bunker was eliminated, creating a wider approach area between the water hazard and the lone bunker on the right. “I think the second shot on 15 is way more exciting and consequential than it was before,” said Maverick McNealy, whose lone career win on the PGA Tour thus far came at the 2024 RSM Classic. I think there's going to be a lot more variance in score because of the water bringing in on the left," said veteran Tour pro Keith Mitchell, a local resident. "I think you'll still see some eagles and birdies, but I think you'll start to see some higher scores as well." item.title: Hamilton picks Verstappen as target for hilarious cheese bazooka attack
item.description: Lewis Hamilton has jokingly named Max Verstappen as the Formula 1 driver he would target with a giant cheese bazooka, following an unusual question from fans during an event in Las Vegas. While the media have been asking drivers more serious questions about their performances, the championship battle and the challenges awaiting them at the Las Vegas Grand Prix , fans have taken a rather different approach, putting Hamilton on the spot with a particularly bizarre question. The seven-time world champion was taking part in a fan event ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix when he was presented with a rather unconventional scenario involving a hypothetical weapon fitted to his Ferrari steering wheel. Asked which driver he would shoot if he had a button capable of firing melted cheese from a giant bazooka, Hamilton initially struggled to settle on a name. "That's a really good question. Who should I blast with cheese? That's pretty funny," the Ferrari driver responded. After someone suggested that a particular driver was already on his mind, Hamilton insisted he was still undecided and turned to the audience for suggestions. "No, I don't know who to pick. Who do you all think would be good?" Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Hamilton rules out Leclerc before settling on Verstappen Verstappen was the first name suggested by the crowd, prompting an amused reaction from Hamilton. "Verstappen?" he repeated, laughing, before asking: "Anyone else?" Another fan proposed Charles Leclerc, but Hamilton immediately ruled out targeting his Ferrari teammate, explaining that their shared responsibilities on the track should take priority. "He's my teammate. I can't say my teammate. We have to win as a team," Hamilton replied. The Briton then floated Lando Norris as another possible target, before someone in the audience suggested Nico Hulkenberg. However, Hamilton was unwilling to pick the German, describing him as harmless. "Nico's harmless. Everyone's saying Max, so maybe I'll go with that. He's probably the closest, so let's cover Max in cheese."

item.title: 'I feel like we're in an Orwell novel right now': Joel Klatt slams CFP selection committee
item.description: Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images, The Joel Klatt Show We got another look at the College Football Playoff selection committee’s rankings on Tuesday, and there is once again plenty to talk about . While there were a few eyebrow-raising decisions across the top 25 — four ranked four-loss SEC teams, Arizona moving up four spots with a loss, Indiana at No. 8 after its shuffling last week — the biggest question mark by a pretty wide margin was the committee’s ranking of No. 3 Alabama relative to No. 5 Texas. There was no great move here, as Alabama held serve at No. 3 with a comfortable win over Vanderbilt, while Texas moved up one spot following its on-the-road win over No. 21 LSU. Instead, it was the lack of movement that was the real news. After the Hoosiers got punished during their bye week, presumably as a result of several of their previous wins taking losses while they were off, many expected the same to happen for the Crimson Tide this week, as Alabama’s five best wins this season all lost this past week. Instead, the committee remained unshaken in its faith in Bama. Joel Klatt, who has never been shy about sharing his opinions on the committee’s rankings, did not hold back while breaking down what he saw as an insult to college football fans. “I feel like we’re in an Orwell novel right now,” Klatt said on Wednesday. “The committee is basically insisting we reject the evidence right before our eyes. Right in front of our faces. It is like their most essential command. “I see the resume between Alabama and Texas. Two spots behind Alabama is Texas, and Texas’ resume is so much better than Alabama’s. Their best wins, Bama, are now Kentucky and South Carolina, who just got the hinges blown off of their front door by Arkansas. … Texas beat Tennessee and Ohio State. A Tennessee team that beat Alabama. There’s no comparing those two resumes. You took a wrong turn, you’re telling us it’s a shortcut, and now you’re just stubborn. Take the crayons away from the committee.” Klatt then imagined a conversation he’d have with a defender of the committee’s current ranking, pointing out the circular reasoning of those that argue in favor of the SEC’s ranked four-loss teams. “The Tide looked very average. ‘Yeah, but hey, it was in the SEC.’ Well, why is that good? ‘Well, because nine teams are ranked.’ Yeah, but why were nine teams ranked? ‘Well, because the SEC is really good.’ Why is the SEC really good? ‘Well, because nine teams are ranked.’ Oh! I wasn’t able to get anything down to recap the win over the New York Jets before midweek hit but had some various thoughts on things from that game and others as well as the upcoming ones that I felt might make for good conversation points. And if not, it’ll make for great conversation starters on telling me why I suck. Let’s do it! If you forgot to look at the score, you’d think the Jets had a good game No, seriously. In fact, if you were casually scanning the box score there’s quite a bit of “evidence” that the Jets had as good of a game as the Bills even. That brings me to one of my favorite Skare-isms; The only stat that matters is the score, and everything else is just context. Yes they had the same number of first downs, nearly equal yards, and the Jets even had slightly better third down conversion rate (both teams were lousy), and a significantly higher time of possession. But none of those things win the game. Both teams had eleven drives. The Jets scored on four of them, and the Bills on five. Which again sounds like a close game. How do these stats add context to the only real stat of the “score?” When it mattered, the Jets’ scoring drives ended in field goals. All but one of the Bills’ scoring drives were touchdowns. You put all that context together and that’s how you translate a box score into a blowout. The NIL and transfer portal had already changed how college programs go after top high school talent, and the incoming 5-in-5 Rule — which grants athletes five years of college eligibility after they enroll at a university — will throw another wrench in the equation. At this point, it takes a special high school recruit to become a priority during a time when coaches would rather build older, more experienced rosters and only have so much money to throw around. Beckham Black is worth it. The younger brother of Orlando Magic guard Anthony Black is the top-rated player in the class of 2027, according to summer RSCI rankings . A 6’4 guard with a 6’7 wingspan, Black is more advanced offensively at this stage than his older brother, showing improved pull-up three-point shooting, advanced live-dribble passing, and tight ball handling over the last year to rise the rankings. Add in Black’s defensive acumen and positional size, and you have the most complete guard in the class of 2027 and a possible top-5 pick in the 2028 NBA Draft. Black remains uncommitted to start his senior year, which is a rarity during a time when 24 of the top-28 recruits in ESPN’s rankings (where Black again sits at No. 1) have already made their college pledge. Black already had the most interesting recruitment in the class even before Arkansas landed Cayden Daughtry on Monday , which added another layer of intrigue to his decision. It wouldn’t be too surprising if Black eventually grew into one of the very best guards in college basketball next year. At this point, his recruiting still remains a big mystery. Here’s how it looks to be shaping up. Arkansas Less than a week ago, Arkansas was named the favorite to land Black by long-time recruiting ace Eric Bossi . It sure feels like Daughtry’s commitment could have changed Black’s plans. For one, Black and Daughtry both think of themselves at point guard, and they didn’t share the floor much during their gold medal run with USA Basketball in the FIBA U19 World Cup. Both players will be in the mix to go top-5 in the 2028 Draft, and they’re both good enough to be the lead guard on a contender next year. Beyond that, Anthony Black — who went to Arkansas under a different coach — posted and deleted the following tweet after news of Daughtry’s commitment broke. Black is big enough to play the two, but does he really view that as his best path for development before jumping to the NBA? I’m skeptical. It sure feels like Arkansas decided to take Daughtry over Black when it became apparent that they could get his commitment, and that’s a totally reasonable decision. Enjoy! Commanders links BE LOUD. WEAR BLACK. pic.twitter.com/EWKbLh1KzK — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 18, 2026 Articles Metro Sports Page Still strapped in, still believing While Jayden was doing his thing on offense, another great story of our season continued Thursday night: Sonny Styles is making an increasingly legitimate run at Defensive Rookie of the Year. His top competition will likely come from his college teammate and fellow NFC East linebacker, Arvell Reese. (Picking at the top of the draft last year had me falling in love with the idea of Reese, Styles or Caleb Downs coming to town. Now they all will, as members of the NFC East, which kind of blows.) Styles edged Reese on the stat sheet with an extra solo tackle and a tackle for loss that Arvell wasn’t able to get. What stands out more than the stats, though, is the tape of that tackle for loss. After positioning his entire team for the play he seemed to know was coming, Styles beat every member of the Giants offense to the spot and brought down J.J. McCarthy for arguably the biggest stop of the game. It led to a 12-yard punt that set up the game-winning drive. Styles continues to impress, displaying the speed, intelligence and tackling ability we sorely need in the middle of our defense. There is still a lot of football to be played, but I believe he is the front-runner for DROY, having put just a sliver of daylight between himself and Reese after Thursday’s game. [W]hat does this all mean in terms of taking care of our business? The margin for error has shrunk to almost nothing, but we do still have some room to work. At 3-5-1, we still have a chance to get to 5-6-1, which is the saddest aspiration I have voiced out loud as a fan in quite some time. That would mean going 2-1 against Cincy, Arizona and Tennessee. That is not an unreasonable expectation, as we should be favored in the last two. The game against Cincinnati is not a “must-win” because we can still navigate our way to a playoff berth with a loss. But at some point, this Commanders team will need to win a game folks might not expect it to win. That opportunity comes this week. Shutting down Joe Burrow would be great, but we have another path: a Jayden gem on offense and, when we need it most, a Sonny Styles impact play. That is the recipe for success in Week 11. item.title: Three White Sox free-agent targets to round out the rotation
item.description: Kris Bubic could give the Sox the best bang for their buck if they move quickly to sign him. | (Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) It’s no secret that the rotation was one of the weakest parts of the White Sox ’s 2026 roster. Chicago’s starters had the fifth-worst ERA (4.60) and the sixth-fewest wins (39). They also made the fewest starts on more than four days’ rest (84) and the most starts on fewer than four days’ rest (24). At the GM meetings in Las Vegas, general manager Chris Getz announced that Grant Taylor will move into the rotation next year, but that’s just the beginning of the rotation renovation. Getz isn’t cooking up his free-agent signings in a silo like a mad scientist, especially now that he’s hired former Brewers assistant director of scouting Matt Roffe as the White Sox director of scouting. Here are a few guys Getz should have on his radar. Kris Bubic If the Sox are ready to pay up for a starter and want someone they know well, Bubic could be their guy. He pitched for the Royals for five and a half years before being traded to the Dodgers in August. In 13 games against the Sox since 2020, he’s posted a 2.60 ERA and allowed 19 earned runs, eight home runs and 24 walks. It shouldn’t take a scout to know that a pitcher who can repeatedly shut down a division rival should be near the top of the free-agent list. Expecting Bubic to pitch at his 2025 level after a rotator cuff strain and a sore elbow was a tall order, but he didn’t disappoint. In 55 innings as a starter and reliever in 2026, he posted a 3.76 ERA, held opponents to a .202 batting average, struck out 56 and allowed just four home runs. That versatility could make him the perfect Swiss Army knife for Will Venable. The Sox need a dependable lefty with experience, and they don’t have to look far. Spotrac estimates Bubic’s market value at $17.4 million per year, nearly the same as the $17.5 million the Sox owe Munetaka Murakami in 2027. Cal Quantrill If Getz has already identified Taylor or Sean Burke as his ace for 2027, bringing in an arm like Quantrill may make sense. After an up-and-down three-year stretch, Quantrill bounced back from minus-0.7 WAR in 2025 to 2.0 in 2026. He lowered his ERA below 3.00 and his WHIP below 1.10 and finished with a winning record. He thrives on inducing soft contact and limiting walks, and his 5.6% walk rate ranked in the 92nd percentile among MLB pitchers in 2026. That combination could make him a good fit at the back of the rotation. Even as he approaches the age when many free agents peak, Quantrill is showing that age doesn’t dictate development. The Sox should take advantage of his late bloom and rocky past to get a fair deal. A two-year contract worth $20 million to $24 million would be appropriate. item.title: Texas A&M women's basketball coach Joni Taylor explains her approach to recruiting after adding three
item.description: Argyle High School forward Landry Murphy is one of three signees with Texas A&M and brings a connection to College Station where her mother, Marth McClelland, played from 1992-95. (Stewart F. House/Special Contributor) COLLEGE STATION - For Joni Taylor, Texas A&M is a destination. That was the language the women's basketball coach used Wednesday afternoon after the Aggies' 59-55 win over East Texas A&M when asked about what she would want in Trev Alberts' successor as the university's next athletic director, but it also provides an interesting window into the way she approaches recruiting. "College Station, Texas A&M is a landing spot," Taylor said. "It's not a jumping-off spot to go somewhere else. And so, the first thing that I'm looking for is someone who wants to be here, have roots here and be an Aggie." On Tuesday, her program announced the signing of three prospects in the 2027 recruiting class - 6-1 forward Landry Murphy of Argyle High School, 5-9 guard Timani Harris of DME Academy (Florida) and 6-1 wing Kie'Aundria "KJ" Acree out of Monroe High School (Georgia). Acree is considered the No. 55 overall prospect by ESPN's 2027 rankings, while Harris is ranked No. 67 nationally. Murphy is unranked but helped Argyle to a 5A Division II State Championship last season. Murphy, a Texas product, gives the class a direct connection to the program's history; the Dallas Morning News' Preseason All-Area Team selection is the daughter of former Aggie Martha McClelland (1992-95), who helped A&M reach its first NCAA Tournament Sweet 16 and hoist the 1995 NWIT Championship trophy. Acree gives Taylor another connection to a state she knows - and has recruited - quite well. Taylor, who spent the first seven seasons as a head coach in Athens, where she led Georgia to four NCAA Tournament appearances and an overall record of 140-75 prior to leaving for A&M in 2022 to replace 2011 national champion and Hall of Fame head coach Gary Blair in 2022. Following signing day, only two top-100 prospects in the class of 2027 remain uncommitted - top-ranked recruit and point guard Kaleena Smith, who recently announced a final three of Arizona State, UCLA and Southern California, and No. 2 overall player, 6-2 wing Ivanna Wilson Manyacka, who dropped a top five of Connecticut, Duke, LSU, Maryland and UCLA over the weekend. Twenty six of the 98 committed top-100 recruits have pledged to SEC programs; regular power and three-time national champion South Carolina and Florida, now led by former Virginia standout player and Rhode Island head coach Tammi Reiss, lead the way with four commitments each. Oklahoma boasts three, while Tennessee, Texas and Vanderbilt join Texas A&M with two apiece. Kentucky, now in its third season under Kenny Brooks, and Alabama, currently in its first season under Pauline Love, are the lone conference teams without a ranked commitment this cycle. item.title: Oakland Coliseum's strange, glorious run is ending: ‘People took pride in the funkiness'
item.description: The Oakland Coliseum, after more than six decades of providing countless memories for countless people, is near the end of its run. (Scott Strazzante/S.F. Chronicle) More than six decades after it first appeared on the Bay Area landscape, an unromantic if functional concrete bowl shrewdly positioned alongside a bustling freeway, the Oakland Coliseum prepares to quietly fade into oblivion, leaving behind a trail of distinctive sports memories. Rickey Henderson raised third base aloft in triumph, Scott Hatteberg launched a walk-off home run for the Athletics' 20th consecutive win, and Derek Jeter improbably flipped the ball home. Raiders quarterback Ken Stabler slung passes to Fred Biletnikoff. The Black Hole overwhelmed opponents. And now the Coliseum's long run as a sports venue - a flawed, funky, historic, occasionally rollicking venue - is almost certainly nearing its end. Rickey Henderson raises third base after setting the all-time stolen-base record on May 1, 1991, during the A's game against the New York Yankees at the Coliseum. The stolen base was Henderson's 939th, moving him past Lou Brock. (Eric Risberg/Associated Press) After years of uncertainty, and barring unexpected snags, the city of Oakland and Alameda County are selling the Coliseum complex to a group of investors known as Oakland Acquisition Company, an affiliate of the African American Sports & Entertainment Group. The window to close the sale officially expires Jan. 30, though the parties involved expect to complete it by Dec. 31. Oakland Acquisition Company plans to split the 112-acre property into two parcels, keeping the larger one - including the aging stadium and most of the expansive parking lot surrounding it. OAC has agreed to sell the smaller, 8½-acre parcel, including the arena where the Golden State Warriors once played, to Oak View Group, an entertainment venue developer and manager. The arena generates profit through concerts and other events, but the stadium has become a financial drag since the Raiders departed after the 2019 season and the A's followed five years later. The Oakland Roots, a minor-league soccer club, played at the Coliseum the past two seasons but will not return there in 2027. "The stadium will require deep subsidies, and the planned buyer has not indicated they will do it," said Henry Gardner, executive director of the Joint Powers Authority, the governing and management body for the city and county. So the Coliseum as we know it is done as a sports venue? "Yeah, I just don't see how it could work," Gardner said. The JPA board passed three resolutions to continue booking and marketing events at the arena through the end of 2028, according to Gardner. There are no similar efforts to bring games, concerts or other events to the stadium. Or, in plainer terms, consider the website listings. item.title: Mizzou’s Final Stretch is Becoming a Test of Commitment
item.description: For the third consecutive season, Missouri Tigers football finds itself playing out the final weeks of November without a College Football Playoff berth within reach. But with two SEC games remaining, starting with Saturday night’s matchup against No. 11 Kentucky, the Tigers still have something to play for. At 6-4, Mizzou was eliminated from playoff contention following last week’s 48-21 loss to No. 1 Georgia. In the first season featuring a nine-game SEC schedule, the expanded 12-team playoff offered a more realistic path for three-loss teams in the conference. The Tigers, however, fell short of that opportunity. Now, the focus shifts toward finding out which players are committed to the grind when there’s not much team glory to play for and building toward next year. Head coach Eli Drinkwitz isn’t interested in making promises about how his team will respond after the devastating loss in Athens. “Words really don’t matter. It’s going to be about actions,” Drinkwitz said Tuesday. “So we can say all the right things, but it’s going to be about us performing at a much better clip than we did.” Mizzou has faced similar circumstances in each of the previous two seasons, with varying results. In 2024, the Tigers dropped a 34-30 decision to No. 21 South Carolina with two regular-season games remaining, eliminating its playoff hopes. Mizzou responded by winning its final three games, including a 27-24 victory over Iowa in the Music City Bowl. Last season, the Tigers’ playoff aspirations ended with a 38-17 loss to Texas A&M with three games left. The Tigers went 2-2 to close the year, defeating Mississippi State and Arkansas while falling to No. 8 Oklahoma and No. 19 Virginia in the Gator Bowl. Last season’s finish left a mixed foundation for the following season, with players such as Ahmad Hardy, Jamal Roberts, Donovan Olugbode and Nicholas Rodriguez returning. Damon Wilson II, Josh Manning, Marvin Burks Jr. and others ultimately transferred. Maintaining a connected locker room and retaining talent has become far more important than a bowl appearance. Many players opt out of bowl games nowadays, making the regular season finish significant. item.title: Colts being 12.5-point underdogs to the 3-6 Texans says it all
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 27: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts fumbles the ball while being tackled during the fourth quarter of the game against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images I keep asking myself if this is rock bottom for the Indianapolis Colts. The disastrous season when Peyton Manning went down was certainly rock bottom. The difference was, with the first overall pick, the franchise had a shovel to dig itself out. There is no shovel. No pick axe. Not even a lantern to lead the way. Being an almost two touchdown underdog to a 3-6 team might be the worst version of rock bottom. The Colts have taken some tremendous shellackings over the years. Those were generally singular moments, though. You have to go back to the beginning of the Indianapolis iteration of the Colts to find many examples of a team this bad. Even then, a debate could be had over who was in worse shape. Those teams had zero expectations. An almost two-decade run of success means there is no turning back. That’s what makes 2026 tough to swallow. The Texans are 3-6. Maybe that’s a tough 3-6, but this team has still lost six times already this year and is expected to whoop the Colts on Thursday Night Football. How did it get so bad? The eternal optimists are probably grinding their teeth right now, but what’s the worst part about next year: the fact the Colts have no direction at quarterback or the fact they won’t have a first-round pick to get one? Having a stockpile of draft picks is only good if the Colts hit. That remains to be seen. For now, they are two touchdown underdogs to the team currently with the ninth overall pick. Ouch . What’s the solution? No clue. Where do the Colts go from here? Not my job to figure out. Ideally, this is rock bottom. Ideally, there is nowhere to go but up. Ideally, the Colts hit on multiple draft picks and can get this thing going again. That’s what we all want, a winner. We want to watch good competitive football. It’s hard to do that when your favorite team is in such a deep hole, though. Nothing left to do but climb.

Pivetta was disappointing in his time with the Red Sox. He had good strikeout numbers, decent fastball velocity, and good peripheral stats. Cam Skattebo, New York Giants Perhaps this was the plan all along, as Skattebo is back to full health and the Giants didn’t add a running back at the Trade Deadline. Everyone else in New York’s backfield falls in behind the second-year running back who has three touchdowns and 202 rushing yards over the past two weeks. It’s likely going to be a tough matchup this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but we don’t have to worry about role here. Bhayshul Tuten, Jacksonville Jaguars Tuten has reached the end zone in three straight weeks, and he has eight touchdowns overall on the season. Jacksonville’s offense is humming right along, and Tuten is a large part of that with 609 rushing yards while averaging 4.1 yards per carry. Beginning in Week 5, Gordon hasn’t had less than 16 carries in a game, and he’s averaging a solid 4.2 yards per carry with 539 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the season. His ceiling is limited as Gordon doesn’t do much in the receiving game, but he also consistently moves the chains, and that counts for something here. 12. Tony Pollard, Tennessee Titans Maybe it’s time to give Pollard some due. Last week, Pollard struggled to find room to run against Jacksonville, with nine carries for 33 yards, but he did catch eight passes for 66 yards and a touchdown. That came after Pollard broke the 100-yard mark in consecutive games while rushing for a combined 236 yards and five touchdowns. 11. Derrick Henry, Baltimore Ravens The hope is that Jacoby Brissett can bring some stability to Baltimore’s offense and, therefore, to Henry.
